benefits_en:
1. The best companion in Allah's sight is the best to his companion, and the best neighbor is the best to his neighbor.
2. True goodness is proven through daily close interpersonal interactions.

1. Do not belittle any neighbor giving a gift to her neighbor, even if it is only the trotter of a sheep.
2. Small gifts foster warmth, mutual affection, and community goodwill.

1. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest; the generous hospitality is for three days, and whatever is beyond that is charity.
2. Exemplary Islamic hospitality and social warmth.

1. A Muslim has six reciprocal rights upon their fellow Muslim: greeting them when meeting, answering their invitation, giving sincere advice when consulted, saying 'Yarhamukallah' when they sneeze and praise Allah, visiting them when sick, and following their funeral when they die.
2. The six essential pillars of Muslim communal solidarity.

1. Spreading peace (Salam): 'Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread peace among yourselves.'
2. The greeting of peace is the foundation of mutual love and communal brotherhood.

1. Greeting both those you know and those you do not know is among the finest practices of Islam.
2. Eradicates social barriers, arrogance, and coldness.

1. When two Muslims meet and shake hands, their sins fall away before they part.
2. Handshakes with warmth and smile melt away minor grievances and sins.

1. It is not permissible for a Muslim to boycott their brother for more than three days, turning away from each other; the better of the two is the one who initiates the greeting.
2. Resolving interpersonal disputes quickly and taking the noble initiative to reconcile.

1. Beware of suspicion (Zann), for suspicion is the most deceitful of speech; do not spy, do not probe into faults, do not compete maliciously, do not envy, and do not hate.
2. Mental purity and refraining from intrusive suspicion.

1. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not oppress him, nor abandon him, nor lie to him, nor despise him.
2. Piety is right here (pointing to the chest three times); it is sufficient evil for a person to despise their Muslim brother.

1. The parable of believers in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion is like that of a single body: if one limb aches, the entire body responds with sleeplessness and fever.
2. Organic global solidarity and empathy across the Muslim Ummah.

1. Believers are like a reinforced structure (Bunyan), each part strengthening and supporting the other (interlocking the fingers).
2. Collective resilience and mutual empowerment in community life.

1. Whoever conceals the fault of a Muslim, Allah will conceal their faults in this world and the Hereafter.
2. Discretion, protecting human dignity, and abstaining from public exposure.

1. Whoever defends the honor of their brother in their absence, Allah will shield their face from Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection.
2. Standing up against backbiting and actively defending absent friends.

1. Assist your brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed: assisting the oppressed by helping them, and assisting the oppressor by restraining them from injustice.
2. Courageous intervention to halt wrongdoing and protect victims.

1. Backbiting (Ghibah) is defined as mentioning your brother in a manner they dislike; if what you say is true it is backbiting, and if not it is slander (Buhtan).
2. Strict prohibition of speaking ill of others behind their backs.

1. The talebearer (Nammam) who spreads malicious gossip to sever relationships between people will not enter Paradise.
2. Guarding against gossip that destroys friendships and marriages.

1. You will find among the worst people on Judgment Day the two-faced person who comes to one group with one face and to another with a different face.
2. Sincerity and consistency of character over duplicity and flattery.

1. Envy (Hasad) consumes good deeds just as fire consumes dry firewood.
2. Purging the heart of resentment over blessings bestowed on others.

1. The strong person is not the one who overpowers others in physical wrestling, but the one who controls himself during moments of anger.
2. True strength is emotional self-mastery and patience under provocation.

1. When a man asked for concise life advice, the Prophet ﷺ repeated three times: 'Do not become angry' (La taghdab).
2. Restraining impulsive anger prevents catastrophic decisions in life.

1. If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down; if the anger leaves him, fine, otherwise let him lie down or perform Wudu.
2. Practical physical de-escalation techniques for anger management.

1. Whoever suppresses their anger when they possess the full power to execute it, Allah will summon them before all creation on Judgment Day and give them their choice of rewards.
2. Magnificent divine honor for self-restraint and forgiveness.

1. Gentleness (Rifq) is never added to anything except that it beautifies it, and is never stripped from anything except that it mars it.
2. Gentleness is the hallmark of prophetic interaction and leadership.

1. Indeed, Allah is Gentle and loves gentleness in all matters, and grants through gentleness what He does not grant through harshness.
2. Winning hearts through patience, soft speech, and kindness.

1. The merciful people will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful; show mercy to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will show mercy to you.
2. Universal compassion toward all living beings as a path to divine grace.

1. Whoever does not show mercy to people, Allah will not show mercy to them.
2. Hardheartedness and cruelty forfeit divine mercy.

1. Kissing children and showing them physical affection: when a man boasted he never kissed his ten children, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'What can I do for you if Allah has removed mercy from your heart?'
2. Nurturing children with warmth, love, and tenderness.

1. The Prophet ﷺ placed his grandson on his lap and kissed him, weeping with tears of mercy: 'This is mercy that Allah has placed in the hearts of His servants.'
2. Natural emotional expression and tears of empathy are signs of soft, living hearts.

1. A woman was punished in Hellfire because of a cat she imprisoned until it died of starvation, neither feeding it nor letting it eat from the earth.
2. Severe accountability for animal cruelty and neglect.

1. A sinful man was forgiven and entered Paradise because he climbed down a deep well, filled his shoe with water, and gave drink to a panting, thirsty dog.
2. Sincere kindness to a suffering animal can earn complete divine pardon.

1. In every living being with a moist liver there is a reward for showing kindness.
2. Boundless scope of Islamic animal welfare and compassion.

1. Indeed, Allah has prescribed excellence (Ihsan) in all things: even when slaughtering an animal, sharpen the blade and relieve the animal's suffering.
2. Humane, ethical standards applied universally even during meat preparation.

1. Do not use any living creature as a target for archery or shooting practice.
2. Strict prohibition of inflicting needless pain on animals for sport.

1. The Prophet ﷺ strictly forbade branding animals on their faces or striking them on the face.
2. Respecting the physical dignity of all creatures created by Allah.

1. Good character (Husn al-Khuluq) is the heaviest thing placed upon the Scale of the believer on the Day of Resurrection.
2. High moral conduct outweighs numerous voluntary acts of worship.

1. The most beloved of you to me and the closest of you to me in station on Judgment Day are the best of you in character.
2. Proximity to the Prophet ﷺ in Paradise is earned through moral excellence.

1. Indeed, I was sent only to perfect and complete noble character traits.
2. The overarching objective of the Prophetic Mission is moral and ethical elevation.

1. The believer reaches through noble character the elevated rank of one who continuously fasts the days and prays the nights.
2. Sublime power of patience, kindness, and cheerful demeanor.

1. Guarantee of a palace on the outskirts of Paradise for one who abandons arguing even when right; a palace in the middle of Paradise for one who abandons lying even in jest; and a palace in the highest part for one with beautiful character.
2. Three guaranteed palaces for three fundamental disciplines of tongue and character.

1. Truthfulness (Sidq) leads to righteousness (Birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise; a person keeps telling the truth until written with Allah as a Siddiq (truthful).
2. Absolute commitment to honesty in all circumstances.

1. Lying (Kadhib) leads to wickedness (Fujur), and wickedness leads to Hellfire; a person keeps lying until written with Allah as a habitual liar.
2. Danger of falsehood corrupting the soul.

1. Fulfill the trust (Amanah) to whoever entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrays you.
2. Unwavering moral integrity that does not stoop to reciprocal betrayal.

1. Honesty and transparency in business: the truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the Prophets, the Siddiqin, and the Martyrs on Judgment Day.
2. Sanctifying marketplace dealings with uncompromising honesty.

1. May Allah show mercy to a person who is lenient and easy-going when selling, buying, and demanding repayment of debts.
2. Flexibility, pleasant mannerisms, and generosity in commercial transactions.

1. Leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt (Da' ma yuribuka ila ma la yuribuk).
2. Cultivating scrupulous piety (Wara') by avoiding ambiguous and doubtful matters.

1. The Halal is clear and the Haram is clear, and between them are ambiguous matters unknown to many people; whoever avoids doubtful matters protects their religion and honor.
2. Spiritual vigilance and staying safely clear of borderline prohibitions.

1. Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which wavers within your chest and you hate for people to find out.
2. The internal moral compass and intuitive conscience of the believer.

1. Consult your heart: righteousness is that with which the soul feels tranquil and the heart feels at rest, even if people repeatedly give you religious verdicts.
2. The sensitivity of the pure heart in discerning moral purity.

1. Modesty (Haya') does not bring anything except goodness, and modesty is entirely good.
2. Haya' is an internal shield preserving dignity and protecting from moral decay.

1. Among the early teachings people preserved from the earlier Prophets: 'If you feel no modesty/shame, then do whatever you wish.'
2. Modesty is the fundamental boundary between civilized human conduct and base animalism.
